fields.question: Does optional visual pretraining mean all vision-specific capacity can be removed?
fields.answer: No. Pretraining priors, dedicated capacity and placement are separate variables. Matched-data and lifetime-budget comparisons still support dedicated visual capacity; it can move from a separate encoder into early backbone layers.
fields.example: A vision-only FFN in early layers adds visual capacity; it is not a fully shared encoder-free model.

fields.question: Why must the visual and shared FFNs consume the same normalized input?
fields.answer: They are parallel additive capacity, not a visual FFN applied after the shared FFN. Extra QKVO and visual-FFN output zero initialization preserve the initial shared function.
fields.example: F(N(h))+DeltaF(N(h)) generally differs from DeltaF(F(N(h))); the latter changes both initialization and dependencies.

fields.question: Do vision-only projections imply separate, mutually invisible image and text attention?
fields.answer: No. The mask gates extra projections and FFNs; QKV still enter one joint attention. Text receives no dedicated branch but can change by reading visual tokens.
fields.example: A zero extra text Q does not prevent attention to visual K/V. Isolating modality attention changes the method.

fields.question: Do initial equivalence and a 16-step MSE reduction establish VQA or TTFT results?
fields.answer: No. They check tensor branches, gradients and causality without image encoding, the full backbone/corpus, or H200 concurrent serving. Capability and speed require separate matched-budget measurements; this component is not Evolve promotion evidence.
fields.example: Fitting a constant offset to random 16-dimensional features is not image question answering. Passing CPU and CUDA checks supplies no end-to-end latency conclusion.

fields.question: Can ArchSpace's M be filled with parameter count?
fields.answer: No. M is training FLOPs per token and C=M times training tokens D. Architectures can have different computation per parameter; replacing M with parameter count breaks both the budget and published coefficient units.
fields.example: Two 1B-parameter architectures can consume different training FLOPs per token and therefore occupy different IsoFLOP points.

fields.question: Why does quadrupling the optimal batch double the conditional optimal LR?
fields.answer: The coupled term cosh(e-b/2) is minimized at e=b/2 for fixed b, yielding eta=eta_star times sqrt(B/B_star). The rho*cosh(b) penalty remains, so a conditional optimum is not the joint optimum.
fields.example: At B=4B_star and eta=2eta_star the coupled term vanishes, but the batch-offset penalty does not.

fields.question: Which variables differ between ArchSpace and Data Mixing Laws?
fields.answer: Data Mixing Laws fits domain mixtures and scale from pilot mixtures. ArchSpace fixes data/tokenization while comparing architecture size and LR/batch budget relationships. Their coefficients cannot be exchanged or data gains attributed to architecture.
fields.example: A new architecture trained on a better mixture has two interventions; its lower loss alone does not isolate architecture benefit.

fields.question: Does the local CoupledLaw perform automatic architecture search?
fields.answer: No. It evaluates two published coefficient sets and an analytic budget optimum, without training candidates, fitting new curves or controlling Evolve. New-architecture applicability, completed LR decay and the fixed eleven-domain protocol still need validation.
fields.example: Returning recommended M and D neither constructs a model nor establishes its predicted loss.

fields.question: Does D-JEPA's information bound show that every multimodal JEPA loses private information?
fields.answer: No. It constrains exactly aligned solutions under its assumptions. Complete models with prediction objectives, private branches or other terms are not directly characterized by that bound.
fields.example: An image containing colors and a counting-only question are not equally informative. Adding private visual prediction means the full objective is no longer alignment-only.

fields.question: Why penalize four private–shared pairs but not the two private fibers?
fields.answer: The terms discourage private information leaking into shared cores while allowing private fibers to coordinate on joint reasoning. Private–private decorrelation changes the objective and can suppress jointly useful signals.
fields.example: Visual attributes and a question's relation selector may occupy separate private branches yet need to combine to answer.

fields.question: Why is one SIGReg on concatenated shared/private features not equivalent?
fields.answer: A concatenated check permits a shortcut where private variance expands while shared features collapse. D-JEPA regularizes each subspace separately and combines them with explicit weights, not a substituted global variance penalty.
fields.example: Near-zero shared features can be hidden by large private features in aggregate statistics; separate checks retain the shared collapse signal.

fields.question: Why is local loss reduction not a reproduction of 39.61% CLEVR accuracy?
fields.answer: Only caller-supplied features, a single-context objective and tiny heads are used. There are no DINO/BERT features, real view sampling, matched probes or PID. Paper Eq.5 normalization also differs from the author's multi-view averaging, so full numerical parity is not claimed.
fields.example: A twelve-step random-feature loss check produces no CLEVR test predictions and therefore no CLEVR accuracy.

fields.question: Does no direct own-space comparison mean DuoJEPA encoders train independently?
fields.answer: No. Translation loss updates both the translator and target centroid, coupling encoder training. It does not directly force the raw own embeddings to coincide.
fields.example: An image translated into text space updates the text positive/negative centroids and thus the text encoder.

fields.question: Can raw global CLS vectors be averaged before one normalization?
fields.answer: The paper applies nonlearned LN and unit normalization per view, sums those vectors, then normalizes again. Averaging raw vectors changes view weights and positive directions when norms or means differ.
fields.example: A raw view with 100 times the other view's norm dominates a raw average; per-view unit normalization prevents that 100-fold weighting.

fields.question: Is a small residual coefficient equivalent to a skipless translator?
fields.answer: No. Skipless removes both identity additions and uses orthogonal/SVD initialization to preserve signal. Any retained identity route can encourage own spaces to move together. Unaligned-space behavior still requires geometric evaluation.
fields.example: Zeroing the final MLP makes a truly skipless output zero; a residual layer can still pass input or an attention residual.

fields.question: Can the target centroid be detached for stability without changing DuoJEPA?
fields.answer: That switches to a separately ablated path. The main objective differentiates through both sides and uses global-device negatives. Local code preserves both gradients but implements only within-batch CLS and one image head, not full LeJEPA/distributed training.
fields.example: Both own_a.grad and own_b.grad should be nonzero after target_space_loss. Detaching prevents this mechanism from updating the target encoder.

fields.question: Does pixel-space generation mean PixVid uses no pretrained latent-model knowledge?
fields.answer: No. It transfers a pretrained latent DiT through offline pixel–latent alignment and timestep calibration, then adds a detailer. Output space and training from scratch are separate choices.
fields.example: Inherited DiT weights with a new patch mapping and detailer still use latent pretraining rather than a fully random model.

fields.question: Is a noise-weighted flow MSE a complete implementation of PixVid's core?
fields.answer: No. Pixel–latent alignment fusion, SNR timestep mapping, patch transfer and the spatiotemporal detailer with its training constraints remain necessary. A generic loss supplies none of those dependencies.
fields.example: Adding inverse-sigma-squared weighting to an arbitrary convolutional model does not import DiT knowledge or correct temporal caches.

fields.question: Why are PixVid and WOVEN different tasks despite using video models?
fields.answer: PixVid studies a generator's latent-to-pixel representation and compute path. WOVEN uses action-conditioned video rollouts as transition supervision for multimodal question answering. Generation quality is not transition reasoning ability.
fields.example: A sharper video can still show the wrong action outcome. Correct transition multiple choice does not establish high-resolution generation.

fields.question: Why not reproduce PixVid if one inference might fit on an A100?
fields.answer: Cost covers the complete training/evaluation campaign, not memory fit alone. The study has a 14B model, about 1.3 million clips, 20k updates and resolution/ablation matrices. It is review DONE without downloads or cost-probing runs.
fields.example: One reported setting needs 192 seconds per clip; hundreds of clips, seeds and training add much more and are not a quick component check.

fields.question: Why retain historical Google attribution but group Spectral Ghost under v4 Georgia Tech?
fields.answer: Affiliation evidence belongs to a version. V1 listed Google DeepMind first for Bo Dai and Dale; reviewed v4 lists Georgia Tech, Harvard and UAlberta only. Matching names do not replace the reviewed byline.
fields.example: The November 10 v4 update is not a first release; January 28 remains the original date. Thanking Google researchers does not establish author affiliation.

fields.question: Why does unbiased VICReg exclude i=j and divide by B(B−1)?
fields.answer: Same-sample terms introduce fourth moments and batch-dependent bias into the squared-covariance plug-in. The U-statistic counts ordered distinct independent pairs, removing that bias under the paper's sampling assumptions.
fields.example: For B=2, only (1,2) and (2,1) remain. Adding (1,1) and (2,2) and dividing by four creates a different estimator.

fields.question: Can contrastive/non-contrastive labels determine the need for large batches?
fields.answer: No. Squared contrastive objectives can be unbiased, ranking NCE optimizes a consistent fixed-negative surrogate, and non-contrastive covariance plug-ins can still be biased. Under misspecification the negative count can also change the optimum.
fields.example: Calling a covariance penalty non-contrastive does not remove same-sample fourth moments. Unbiasedness does not guarantee low variance.

fields.question: Why label this a theory review instead of an expensive unreplicated experiment?
fields.answer: Fixed v4 reports no unified empirical campaign to rerun and explicitly leaves those ablations to future work. Inventing its model, data or GPU cost would be misleading. This intake has theoretical discussion only, without implementation, metrics, GPU receipts or automatic tasks.
fields.example: A new objective does not imply the authors trained an 8B model. No training configuration means no fabricated deferred-experiment table.
